recommended.title: The authentication rate-limit policy is Better Auth's default, which nobody in this project chose
recommended.acceptance:
FOUND BY ACCIDENT, WHICH IS THE POINT. PL-0715 was opened because the watchlist e2e harness read a rate-limited sign-UP as a wrong password and reported a product failure. Repairing the harness was correct and is DONE. It did not answer the question the defect exposed: this product has never DECIDED what its authentication rate-limit policy is.

WHAT IS TRUE TODAY, read from the dependency rather than asserted. better-auth 1.7.5 sets `enabled: options.rateLimit?.enabled ?? isProduction` (dist/context/create-context.mjs:172), so throttling is ON in production and OFF in development -- the two deployments this project runs its e2e suite against answer sign-in differently, and neither answer was chosen here. `getDefaultSpecialRules` then applies a window of 10s and a max of 3 to any path beginning /sign-in or /sign-up, keyed per IP and path. Nothing in this repository names any of those numbers, so nobody has weighed them and a dependency bump can change the product's brute-force posture silently.

REQUIRED: the policy is STATED IN THIS REPOSITORY -- window, maximum, key, and which paths -- so a reader can see what the product does without reading node_modules, and so a Better Auth upgrade that changes a default is a diff rather than a surprise.
REQUIRED: the reasoning is written down, including why the chosen numbers are the chosen numbers. A credential-stuffing attacker and a family of four sharing one IP are both real; this must say which way it errs and why.
REQUIRED: the development/production divergence is decided deliberately rather than inherited. If throttling stays off in development, that is a defensible choice and must be written as a choice; a suite that can only pass because a control is absent is a suite that does not test the shipped product.
REQUIRED: the behaviour is asserted by a test that distinguishes a RATE-LIMITED refusal from a WRONG-CREDENTIAL refusal. That confusion is the whole origin of this task and it must not be able to come back silently.

MUST NOT: weaken the control. Raising the ceiling, widening the window, or disabling throttling to make a test or a harness easier is forbidden outright -- if a harness is inconvenienced, the harness changes, which is exactly what PL-0715 did.
MUST NOT: expose a bypass of any kind -- no header, no environment variable, no test-only path that turns the limiter off in a deployment that ships.

OUT OF SCOPE: CAPTCHA, account lockout, device fingerprinting, IP reputation, and any other new control. This task is about NAMING AND OWNING the policy that is already in effect, not about adding defences.
recommended.notes:
FILED IN ROUND 109 at gpt-architect's instruction, which asked for a narrowly-scoped security task 'if one does not already exist' and said not to change the security behaviour inside PL-0715. Board searched before filing: PL-0715 (DONE) repaired the harness, PW-0312 (DONE) and PW-0403 (DONE) built authentication entry and production session resolution, and none of the three names a rate-limit policy in acceptance or notes. No open task holds it.

Conflict-checked in both fields in both directions at filing. Active tasks are PL-0714 (REVIEW, .github/workflows/ci.yml), PW-0208 (REVIEW, apps/desktop/**), PW-0307 (REVIEW, named apps/web and e2e files), PW-0310 (IN_PROGRESS, apps/web/src/lib/a11y/**, globals.css, two test files) and PW-0602 (IN_PROGRESS, .github/workflows/windows.yml). None names apps/web/src/lib/auth in either field. e2e/src/identity.ts is listed here as a REVIEW DEPENDENCY and deliberately not as an allowed path: this task must be readable against the harness it came from without reserving a file it has no reason to write.

P1 rather than P0: the control is PRESENT and the posture is not currently open. What is absent is the decision, which is what makes it silent and what makes a dependency bump dangerous.
